chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Jamil, from Abdullah ibn Muhammad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him: A man left behind his daughter and his sister (paternal) to his father and mother. He said: 'All the wealth belongs to his daughter.'

key_terms.لِأَبِيهِ وَأُمِّهِ: to his father and mother (indicating their presence as heirs)

ai.seo_question: Who inherits the entire estate when a man leaves behind a daughter, father, mother, and paternal sister?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that a daughter takes the entire estate when she is the sole child, effectively excluding the father, mother, and paternal sister. This ruling highlights the principle of *hujb* (exclusion) in Shia jurisprudence, where the presence of a direct descendant can supersede other relatives, contrasting with some Sunni schools where the father might retain a share. The hadith underscores the primacy of the daughter as a primary heir in the absence of sons, reflecting the Quranic distribution of fixed shares (*fara'id*).
